title: Derived pushforward commutes canonically with strict tower inverse limit
statement:
Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),R)\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),S)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi on small sites, with structural ring map $f^{-1}S\to R$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and K-injective total derived direct image [def-pur-kinjective-complex, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. For $T=R,S$ put $\operatorname{Tow}(T)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\operatorname{Mod}(T))$, the category of strict inverse sequences with levelwise exactness. Let $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ apply module direct image levelwise and let $Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$ be its total right derived functor. Write $L_R,L_S$ for total right derived inverse limit of strict towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. For every $M\in D(\operatorname{Tow}(R))$, there are natural evaluation identifications $\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M\cong Rf_*\operatorname{ev}_nM$ and a canonical natural isomorphism
$$a_{f,M}:Rf_*L_R(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_S(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M).$$
The comparison is the one induced by the equality of underived composite direct images $f_*\lim_R=\lim_S f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$: regard inverse limit as direct image from the tower ringed topos and compare both derived composites with the total derived functor of that common direct image. Under the evaluation identifications, it commutes with all tower projections. No boundedness, constructibility, exact countable products, or identification $f^{-1}S=R$ is assumed.

proof.text: Set $\mathcal C_R=\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal C_S=\mathcal D$. For $T=R,S$, form the small tower site $\mathcal C_T\times\mathbf N_{\geq1}$: an arrow $(U,n)\to(V,m)$ consists of $U\to V$ and $n\leq m$, and coverings have a fixed integer and are coverings of the original site. A sheaf is exactly a strict inverse sequence, since the sheaf condition is imposed separately at each integer; put the constant-in-the-integer ring sheaf $T^{\operatorname{Tow}}(U,n)=T(U)$. Its module sheaves are exactly $\operatorname{Tow}(T)$, with the actions and restriction maps of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The morphism $g_T$ to the original ringed topos has constant-tower inverse image, identity structural ring map, and direct image $\lim_T$: a map from the constant tower on $V$ to $H_\bullet$ is precisely a compatible family $V\to H_n$. Apply the underlying geometric inverse image and direct image of $f$ levelwise to get $F=f\times1$ on tower topoi. Their adjunction restricts to tower maps because its bijections are natural in each transition; levelwise inverse image preserves finite limits. Give $F$ the levelwise structural maps $f^{-1}S\to R$. Its module direct image is $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$. The square $fg_R=g_SF$ is a square of ringed topoi: on inverse images, both routes send a sheaf to the constant tower on $f^{-1}$ of that sheaf, with the same structural map. Consequently the composite module direct images are canonically identified, $f_*\lim_R=\lim_S f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$. This identification sends $f_*p_n$ to the $n$-th limit projection; it is also obtained by the displayed compatible-family adjunction.

proof.text: Represent $M$ by a complex $C$ of $R$-towers. On the small ringed tower site, [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] gives a K-injective resolution $C\to I$. Thus $Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M$ is represented by the strict tower complex $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}I$. By [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective], $I_n$ is K-injective. Since exactness in towers is levelwise, $C_n\to I_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism, and $f_*I_n$ computes $Rf_*\operatorname{ev}_nM$. Hence $\operatorname{ev}_nRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M$ and $Rf_*\operatorname{ev}_nM$ have the same representative $f_*I_n$. The transitions on both sides are $f_*(I_{n+1}\to I_n)$, so these evaluation identifications respect every transition.

proof.text: The constant-tower functor $\Delta_T$ is additive and exact, since exactness is levelwise. The compatible-family bijection in Step 1 gives $\Delta_T\dashv\lim_T$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to conclude that $\lim_T$ sends K-injective tower complexes to K-injective module complexes. In particular $\lim_R I$ is K-injective and represents $L_R M$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], so $f_*\lim_R I$ represents $Rf_*L_R M$. Choose a K-injective tower resolution $j:f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}I\to J$ over $S$, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Then $\lim_SJ$ represents $L_S(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M)$. Evaluation gives K-injective $J_n$ by [lem-weil-tower-evaluation-kinjective], and $j_n:f_*I_n\to J_n$ is a quasi-isomorphism. No assertion that $f_*I$ or $f_*I_n$ is K-injective is needed.

proof.text: Put $P=fg_R=g_SF$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to $(g_R,f)$ and $(F,g_S)$, which are morphisms of small ringed topoi by Step 1. This gives natural isomorphisms $\kappa_{f,g_R}:RP_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*L_R$ and $\kappa_{g_S,F}:RP_*\xrightarrow{\sim}L_SRf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$. Define $a_f=\kappa_{g_S,F}\circ\kappa_{f,g_R}^{-1}$ using the common-direct-image identification of Step 1. Its normalization is explicit: on $I$, the first comparison is represented by the identity of $f_*\lim_RI$, since $\lim_RI$ is already K-injective; the second is represented by $\lim_Sj:\lim_S f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}I\to\lim_SJ$. The normalization clause of the cited node says that this second map is a quasi-isomorphism. Therefore $a_{f,M}$ is represented by that map after the underived identification, and is an isomorphism with exactly the common-direct-image normalization required in the statement.

proof.text: Write $p_n:\lim_RI\to I_n$ and $q_n:\lim_SJ\to J_n$ for the strict projections. Naturality of ordinary inverse limit gives the equality of chain maps $q_n\circ\lim_Sj=j_n\circ f_*p_n$, after the Step 1 identification. The projection from $L_S(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M)$ to $\operatorname{ev}_n(Rf_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}M)$ is represented by $q_n$, with that target represented by $J_n$. To express the target using the representative $f_*I_n$ from Step 2, use the inverse of the quasi-isomorphism $j_n:f_*I_n\to J_n$. Thus in the derived category $j_n^{-1}q_na_{f,M}=f_*p_n$. Both $\lim_RI$ and $I_n$ are K-injective by Steps 2 and 3, so $f_*p_n$ represents $Rf_*$ of the $n$-th projection from $L_RM$. This proves compatibility with every projection, including its specific evaluation identification. The equality is an equality of chain maps before localization, rather than a choice of a morphism between abstract cone triangles.

proof.text: The comparisons in Step 4 are natural in $M$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. For the evaluation identifications, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents a derived morphism between two resolved towers by a chain map $u:I\to I'$ uniquely up to homotopy. Evaluating and applying $f_*$ gives $f_*u_n$ on both representatives in Step 2, and preserves homotopies termwise. The same cited node says that two K-injective resolutions are related by homotopy equivalences; evaluation, $f_*^{\operatorname{Tow}}$, and inverse limit preserve those equivalences because their additive termwise actions preserve the homotopy equation. Hence the evaluation identifications are canonical and natural, and the projection equality in Step 5 is independent of all resolution choices. Smallness ensured the resolutions; nowhere was boundedness, product exactness, constructibility, or exactness of module $f^*$ used.
